messages:
Maya: Heads up — Customer X reports ~30% of hosted API calls returning 502s since ~09:02 UTC, only affects model inference route /v1/generate. Saw spike in errors after the key-rotation window at 09:00.
Dmitri: Copy. Any trace IDs or sample request ids?
Maya: Sample trace: trace=trc-7f3a, request id: req-4b2f. I pulled gateway logs: multiple upstream resets with 'upstream prematurely closed connection' from auth-proxy.
Ben: Noted. Is it only customers using session affinity/cookie-based auth?
Maya: Customer X uses sticky sessions (session cookie + edge sticky routing). We also saw 504s for some long polling clients but most are 502s.
Jules: Pasting relevant nginx/edge snippet I grabbed: 
```
[edge-proxy] 2024-02-09T09:03:12Z "GET /v1/generate" 502 upstream: "http://auth-proxy:8080/verify" error: "recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)" host: api.redwood.example
```
Maya: auth-proxy logs show a burst of 429s from internal billing checks at the same time, then the auth process closes keepalive connections.
Dmitri: That would explain connection churn. If auth closes sockets during rotation, nginx/Envoy pool might hit max_active and start returning 502s.
Ben: Could also be a TLS session cache miss after key rotation causing renegotiation TTLs. Any TLS handshake errors?
Maya: I don't see TLS handshake fails in edge logs — mostly RSTs and upstream EOFs.
Jules: Repro steps I'm running locally: 
```bash
# hammer auth endpoint to simulate rotation load
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Cookie: session=sticky123" https://edge.redwood.internal/v1/generate &
done
```
This reproduces a 5-10% 502 rate and a lot of `recv() failed (104)` in proxy.
infra-bot: Deploybot: canary rollout for auth-proxy v2.14 started at 09:00 UTC. 12/24 pods updated.
Maya: That matches timing — canary started at 09:00, key rotation + new auth container behaviour may be closing keepalives.
Dmitri: Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback canary to previous auth-proxy image, 2) increase upstream keepalive pool, 3) temporarily disable sticky session affinity for the route to spread load.
Ben: Also check billing service rate limiter — if it returns 429s mid-auth check, auth-proxy might short-circuit and close. We should throttle calls or add exponential backoff in auth-proxy.
Jules: I've opened a quick alert on billing svc CPU and rate limiter counters — it's spiking. Might be coincident with an external tenant activity burst.
Maya: Customer is panicking — requesting ETA.
Dmitri: Start with rollback of canary to stop new behaviour. I'm patching deployment now.
infra-bot: Deploybot: rollback auth-proxy to v2.13 initiated (patch-rollback).
Maya: After rollback see error rate trending down to baseline in the last 90s.
Ben: Good. Next steps: post-mortem to cover sticky session interaction with auth connection semantics, and add a small change to auth-proxy to use graceful keepalive drain instead of immediate close during rotation.
Jules: I'll capture a repro run and attach request traces + curl output to the ticket. Also recommend increasing nginx upstream_keepalive size from 16 -> 64 for the route as a short term improvement.
Maya: Customer confirmed degraded but usable, thanks. I'll leave the thread open for root cause and CR.
support-bot: Created ticket #SUP-8421 and linked customer case.
Dmitri: Recording RCA notes: probable root cause = canary auth-proxy image that aggressively closed persistent connections during key rotation; secondary factor = billing rate limiter spikes causing auth to return transient 429s.
Ben: Action items: (a) fix auth-proxy keepalive drain, (b) add rate-limited retry in edge for auth verification to avoid hard 502s, (c) update runbook for canary key rotations to include small ramp and auth health checks.
Maya: Will follow up with customer and schedule postmortem doc. Closing if no new errors in 30m. :thumbsup:
